claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure comprising deformation twins and precipitates.
Introducing deformation twins and precipitates enhances the work-hardening capability of HfNbTiVAl10.
Introducing deformation twins and precipitates enhances the yield strength of HfNbTiVAl10.
The hierarchical heterostructure maintains the tensile ductility of HfNbTiVAl10 while increasing its strength.
Precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase yield strength.
Deformation twinning produces a TWIP effect that increases work hardening.
Deformation twinning can improve tensile ductility.
A sufficiently high work-hardening rate stabilizes tensile flow at high yield strength.
The proposed heterostructure improves the predictive accuracy of Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture-related behavior relative to established simulations.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to materials with low stacking-fault energies.
Reduced dislocation mobility and storage capacity can cause severe strain localization.
Severe strain localization can cause loss of tensile ductility and early plastic instability.
Introducing both deformation twins and precipitates may cause severe strain localization in HfNbTiVAl10.

contradictions.description: The initial material is already described as having the hierarchical heterostructure, while the intervention is the introduction of the deformation twins and precipitates that define that heterostructure. The untreated and treated states are therefore not clearly distinguished.
